jobs.prompt:
FILE ACCESS: your six declared outputs (tools/verify-provenance.mjs, tools/om-manifest-guard.mjs, tools/swarm/core-51.mjs, tools/swarm.mjs, tools/scope-commands.mjs, tests/verify-provenance.test.mjs) are in your worktree and you MAY read and edit them; 'read only the files in your context' means context plus your own outputs. Two earlier attempts stopped as blocked before writing anything (output access; then not knowing where run manifests are saved, now answered in step 4). Only return blocked for a real design conflict.

Goal g-e19bbb50 (release train 2): let the orchestrator gate allow a shell verify job ONLY when the runner itself rebuilt it from the approved ticket ledger (provenance), instead of refusing every shell job under orchestrator mode.

Today: under CLAUDECODE=1 with orchestrator mode on, orchestratorManifestGate / vetManifestBody (tools/om-manifest-guard.mjs) refuses every job with shell: true or a model ending in -shell. Shell verify jobs come from ticketsToManifest (tools/ticket-manifest.mjs) using verifyJobFields (tools/verify-config.mjs: agent claude => shell true). prepareScopeRun (tools/scope-commands.mjs ~line 4055) writes them into docs/scope/waves/wave-*.json, so a wave with a claude verify job can never run under the orchestrator. A hand-written manifest must still never get a shell job past the gate.

Design (follow it; if something in the code makes it impossible, return blocked with the reason, do not invent another design):
1. NEW tools/verify-provenance.mjs owns provenance. It keeps a module-private WeakSet of job objects it rebuilt; export isProvenancedVerifyJob(job) (membership test only; nothing else can add to the set) and async expandVerifyTicketJobs(root, manifest).
2. Wave file shape: in prepareScopeRun, a job that ended up with shell: true (or a -shell model) is written into the wave file as exactly { "id": "<ticket id>", "verifyTicket": "<ticket id>" } (id equals verifyTicket). Every other job is written exactly as today. Move the options prepareScopeRun passes to ticketsToManifest (verify, quality, packageManager, contextEnv, laneModels, scope, ledger, lessons) into one exported helper in scope-commands.mjs so prepareScopeRun and expandVerifyTicketJobs build them identically.
3. expandVerifyTicketJobs(root, manifest): returns the manifest unchanged when no job has verifyTicket. Otherwise: strict keys - a job carrying verifyTicket must have exactly the keys id and verifyTicket, both non-empty strings, id === verifyTicket; any other key (a prompt, shell, agent, model, outputs, ...) refuses. Duplicate job ids in the manifest refuse. Read the ledger (readLedger from tools/tickets.mjs); refuse if missing or !isApproved(ledger). The ticket must exist and have status in DELIVERABLE_STATUSES (tools/tickets.mjs; note prepareScopeRun has already moved wave tickets to running) - done, cancelled, proposed, review or unknown tickets refuse. Rebuild that one ticket's job with ticketsToManifest([ticket], { ...same options, ready: false }) and take the job with that id; if no job or it is not a shell job, refuse. Add the rebuilt object to the WeakSet and put it in place of the compact entry. Refusals throw an Error with code 'verify-provenance-refused' and a message naming the job id and the reason.
4. Runner (the coordinator located these sites for you; tools/swarm.mjs is now one of your outputs): (a) expandVerifyTicketJobs is idempotent (no verifyTicket keys => returns the input unchanged). Call it at the top of validateProject in tools/swarm/core-51.mjs before the first validateManifest, so preflight/validate/scaffold callers work on compact manifests. (b) In runManifest (tools/swarm.mjs ~line 586) expand BEFORE anything reads manifest.jobs, but save the COMPACT form to .swarm/runs/<id>/manifest.json at both jsonWrite sites (~586 and ~626), so resume re-reads the compact form and expands again (fresh ledger check, fresh WeakSet marks). Check the resume path (resumeState) reaches the same expansion. Make sure integrate/inspect/status readers of the saved manifest.json (tools/swarm/core-51.mjs ~221, core-52.mjs, core-62.mjs call validateManifest on it) still work with compact jobs: either they expand too or they read job ids/outputs from state.json - choose the smaller safe change and say which. (c) tools/swarm.mjs ~747 re-validates one job as { ...job, after: undefined } on a provider fallback; that copy would lose the provenance mark. Keep it working without letting a copy become trusted by accident: e.g. pass the original job object when 'after' is already absent, or export from verify-provenance.mjs a function that marks a shallow copy ONLY when the source object is already marked. (d) The wave-prep validate callbacks at tools/swarm.mjs ~3097 and ~3142 do JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(manifest)) then validateManifest(copy) then validateProject(root, copy). prepareScopeRun must hand them the compact form it will write, and they must call validateProject (which expands) instead of validateManifest first. Note prepareScopeRun holds the scope lock while validate runs: expansion only reads the ledger, never takes that lock, so no deadlock; confirm that. State in your summary what you did for (b), (c) and (d).
5. Gate: in vetJobs (tools/om-manifest-guard.mjs) a job with shell: true or a -shell model is allowed only when isProvenancedVerifyJob(job) is true; everything else about that job (its setup/checks argvs) is still vetted as today. omRunManifestVetted (sync, reads the file) must refuse a compact job that has any extra key, and otherwise leave compact jobs for the runner. The gate runs inside applyManifestJobTypes before jobs are copied, so the same object identity reaches it; keep it that way and do not spread/copy jobs between expansion and the gate.
Tests in NEW tests/verify-provenance.test.mjs (first line: import './_isolate-config.mjs';), using a temp project with an approved ledger built through the real tickets.mjs/scope helpers and a profile whose verify agent is claude (shapes like the agent-data-business or parts-request-photos profiles: a test command with the {tests} token):
- allowed: a generated compact verify job expands and passes orchestratorManifestGate with CLAUDECODE=1 and orchestrator mode + hook on (stub those the way tests/om-manifest-guard.test.mjs does);
- refused: a compact job with a changed or extra key (prompt, shell, agent), a ticket that is done, cancelled, or proposed, a duplicate id, an unapproved ledger, and a hand-written full shell job (shell: true with a prompt) - the gate still refuses it with code orchestrator-manifest-unvetted;
- prepareScopeRun writes the compact form for a shell verify ticket and the full form for a non-shell ticket.
Do not touch any other file. Existing tests named in your context must keep passing unchanged. Keep the edits small and in the surrounding code's style.

The ignored tests cover scope, runner and gate behaviour that must not change; the coordinator runs the main ones as checks and the full suite before ship.
